kernel-gpu.d: A function compiled to run on thousands of threads on the GPU. The CPU does not execute it: it only enqueues a launch with the grid size, the pointers and the parameters.

stream-cuda.d: A GPU work queue: kernels and copies on the same stream run in order; different streams can overlap if there are free resources.

cta.d: Cooperative Thread Array: a group of threads (in warps of 32) that runs entirely on a single SM and shares its shared memory. A launch grid is a set of CTAs.

ocupacao.d: How many CTAs (or warps) fit on an SM at the same time, limited by the registers, the shared memory and the threads each CTA asks for.

onda-de-ctas.d: A batch of CTAs that the GPU runs simultaneously. With more CTAs than SMs × occupancy, the kernel runs in several waves, and the last one is often partly empty (the tail effect).

intensidade-aritmetica.d: FLOPs executed per byte read from memory. Compared with the GPU's ridge \(P/B\) (~458 FLOP/B on the GB10, BF16), it tells you whether the kernel is memory-bound or compute-bound.

memory-bound.d: A kernel whose time is dominated by reading/writing bytes: the SMs wait for data. It is the regime of decode with small M.

compute-bound.d: A kernel whose time is dominated by arithmetic: above the roofline ridge. It is the regime of prefill with large M.

dispatch-por-m.d: Choosing the kernel according to the number of rows (tokens) the GEMM has in the step: weight-only for small M (decode), BF16/native FP4 for large M (prefill). E.g., GLM53_KDA_BF16_LARGE_M (M > 512).

tiling.d: Splitting a GEMM into blocks (tiles) that each CTA computes, bringing slices of A and B into shared memory and reusing each element many times before discarding it.

shared-memory.d: Fast memory inside each SM, shared by the threads of a CTA and managed by the programmer; organized into 32 banks of 4 bytes.

cp-async.d: An instruction for asynchronous copies from global memory to shared memory that bypass the registers; it lets several slices stay in flight at once (a multi-stage pipeline).

ldmatrix.d: An instruction that loads matrix fragments from shared memory into a warp's registers, already in the layout the tensor core expects.

mma-sync.d: The per-warp matrix multiply-accumulate instruction on the tensor core (e.g., m16n8k16 FP16 → FP32). It is the path on SM121 (GB10), which lacks the tcgen05 of datacenter Blackwell.

epilogo.d: The final part of a GEMM kernel, after the loop over K, while the accumulator is still in registers: a cheap place to apply a scale, an activation, a rotation or a routing weight before writing out.

swizzle.d: A permutation of shared memory addresses (typically XOR-ing the column with bits of the row) so the threads of a warp land on different banks and their accesses are not serialized.

spill.d: When a kernel needs more registers than exist, the compiler dumps values into local memory (LDL/STL instructions), which is slow. GLM's FAST kernel eliminated 39 LDL.

atomics-vetoriais.d: 16-byte atomic operations (e.g., atomicAdd on float4, sm_90+) that accumulate several values into global memory at once; used by GLM's E3 to sum the experts' outputs.

fusao-de-kernels.d: Doing the work of several kernels in one, so intermediate tensors stay in registers/SMEM instead of going to DRAM; it saves bandwidth and launches.

flashattention.d: An algorithm and family of kernels that compute attention in blocks with online softmax, without materializing the score matrix; exact, not approximate. On SM12x, the FA2 version is available.

softmax-online.d: Computing softmax in blocks while keeping only the partial maximum \(m\), the normalizer \(\ell\) and the accumulator \(o\), rescaled by \(e^{m-m'}\) whenever a larger maximum shows up.

split-k.d: Dividing the reduction axis (in decode, the keys) into partitions computed by independent CTAs and then merging the partials; it provides parallelism when there are few rows. In attention, the merge uses log-sum-exp.

log-sum-exp.d: \(\ln \sum_j e^{s_j} = m + \ln \ell\). Storing the LSE of each partition makes it possible to combine partial softmaxes exactly.

backend-de-atencao.d: The implementation vLLM plugs into an attention layer (KV layout, prefill and decode kernels, metadata, CUDA graph support), chosen by capability, head size, KV dtype and attention type.

triton.d: A Python language/compiler for block-based GPU kernels: you write a program (one instance of the kernel, which becomes a CTA) that operates on whole tiles with tl.load/tl.dot; tl.program_id tells you which piece is yours, and the compiler splits the tile among num_warps warps and generates the pipeline (num_stages). JIT-compiled; tl.constexpr parameters produce specialized variants.

flashinfer.d: A kernel library for LLM inference (paged attention, MLA and sparse-MLA, sampling, CUTLASS MoE), with JIT and autotuning. It provides the only sparse-MLA backend in stock vLLM for SM12x (FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120, GLM image); b12x brings its own SM120 sparse-MLA kernels, opt-in in DeepSeek.

flashmla.d: DeepSeek's MLA attention kernels (dense and sparse), designed for Hopper and datacenter Blackwell (SM100); on the GB10, DeepSeek-V4 uses its own SM120 implementation.

marlin.d: A mixed-precision GEMM kernel (4- or 8-bit weights × FP16/BF16 activations) optimized for small batches: it repacks the weights at load time into the tensor core's fragment layout, dequantizes in registers via bit tricks (lop3) and uses a 16-bit MMA. Fast in decode, slow in prefill; it requires aligned dimensions.

cutlass.d: NVIDIA's C++ template library for high-performance GEMMs: tile, stages and epilogue are parameters, and it assembles the “collective” mainloop and epilogue (carried out jointly by the CTA's threads). CuTe is its layout layer (shape:stride), which says which thread touches which element. The basis of FlashInfer CUTLASS's FP4/FP8 kernels.

cutedsl.d: A Python version (DSL) of CuTe for writing CUTLASS-style kernels with JIT compilation; it is the basis of b12x.

skinny-gemm.d: A GEMM with a very small M (1–4 rows, typical of batch-1 decode): almost a GEMV, limited by how fast the weights can be read.

fused-moe.d: An implementation of a Mixture-of-Experts layer in a few launches (routing, permutation, expert GEMMs and finalize), instead of a per-expert loop.

grouped-gemm.d: A single kernel that runs many GEMMs of different sizes (one per expert), reading from a table on the device where each problem starts.

thin-fat-experts.d: Thin: experts with few rows in the step (decode), where what matters is reading the weights fast. Fat: experts with many rows (prefill; the hottest one shows up in almost every token), where math dominates.

host-sync.d: A point where the CPU waits for the GPU in order to read a value (e.g., .item(), .tolist(), nonzero()); it costs CPU time and prevents CUDA graph capture.

graph-safe.d: Code that can be captured in a CUDA graph: no synchronization with the CPU, no dynamic allocation, and the same sequence of kernels on every replay.

moe-cooperativo.d: A GLM decode kernel that groups the slots that picked the same expert as rows of an MMA (stage A gate/up, stage B down), with completion counters; it reads each expert once per run.

b12x.d: A library of CuTeDSL kernels for consumer Blackwell (SM120/121), used by DeepSeek in the MXFP4 W4A16 MoE, in mHC, in the compressed/sparse MLA and in the WO projection.

autotuning.d: Running a kernel's candidate tactics (tiles, splits, warps) at the real shape, picking the fastest and storing it in a hash-keyed cache; under TP it must be consistent across ranks.

jit-aot.d: AOT: the kernel is compiled in the image build for the exact architecture. JIT: it is compiled the first time a shape shows up (Triton, CuTeDSL, TileLang, DeepGEMM, FlashInfer), with an on-disk cache.

tilelang.d: A tile-based kernel DSL compiled by JIT; DeepSeek-V4 uses it in the fused hyper-connection kernels (mHC).

deepgemm.d: DeepSeek's JIT kernel library for FP8/FP4 GEMMs, the sparse indexer's MQA logits and MegaMoE; it names implementations by exact compute capability (hence the sm121 → sm120 alias).

especializacao.d: Generating one compiled variant per value of a constant parameter (tl.constexpr) or per pointer alignment; it multiplies the entries in the JIT cache and can trigger compilation in the middle of serving.

pdl.d: A Hopper+ feature that lets a kernel start its prologue while the previous one finishes, waiting at an explicit point (griddepcontrol.wait) before reading its results. Turned off on SM12x by GLM, which recorded a race with the KDA state kernels.

cuda-cpp.d: C++ with NVIDIA extensions in which you write the code for one thread (blockIdx, threadIdx) and explicitly control SMEM, barriers and tensor cores (inline PTX). Compiled by nvcc, usually at build time (AOT) for an exact architecture, as a PyTorch .so extension.

lane-de-runtime.d: Each of the three execution stacks of the DeepSeek repository: A = the Anemll 0.1.1 image (default production, attention code outside the repo), B = the Stage-C overlay (complete, readable code), C = official-main (experiment). Several envs and files exist in only one lane.

kernel-row-independent.d: A kernel whose result for a row has the same bits whatever the number and content of the other rows in the call: the split-K partition and the summation order are fixed by the weight's shape, with no float atomics. It is what lets TensorFold guarantee drafted = serial and concurrent = solo (batch invariance).

ordem-de-lancamento.d: The order in which the blocks of a grid are dispatched, which roughly follows the linear index, with blockIdx.x varying fastest. Choosing which dimension goes in x decides which blocks run together and, therefore, what is still in L2 when a block rereads a neighbor's data.

prefetch-l2.d: Asking the memory system to bring data into the L2 cache before it is used, without moving it into registers (cp.async.bulk.prefetch.L2, prefetch.global.L2). It changes no result, only when the bytes arrive.

carga-nao-coerente.d: A read through the GPU's read-only path, valid for data that no kernel writes during the call; with L1::no_allocate, it does not fill L1 with data that is read once. At 16 B per lane (.v4.u32), it needs 4× fewer load instructions than 32-bit words.
